summary: The implementation adds startswith/endswith methods but has a critical bug: the hash value doesn't include the prefix/suffix parameter. This causes different prefixes to have the same hash, making queries with different prefixes considered equal and breaking the query cache (returning wrong results). The fix is to include the prefix/suffix in the hashval tuple, similar to how the matches() method includes regex and flags.

checks.claim: startswith/endswith basic functionality works for string matching
checks.evidence: python -c "from tinydb import TinyDB, where; db=TinyDB(':memory:'); db.insert_multiple([{'name':n} for n in ['Alice','Alan','bob']]); assert [d['name'] for d in db.search(where('name').startswith('Al'))] == ['Alice','Alan']"

python -c "from tinydb import TinyDB, where; db=TinyDB(':memory:'); db.insert_multiple([{'name':5},{'name':None},{'x':1},{'name':'Al'}]); assert [d['name'] for d in db.search(where('name').startswith('A'))] == ['Al']"

checks.claim: Different prefixes produce different query results but same hash (BUG)
checks.evidence: python -c "from tinydb import where; q1=where('name').startswith('Al'); q2=where('name').startswith('Bo'); print('hash equal:', hash(q1)==hash(q2), 'q1==q2:', q1==q2)" -> hash equal: True, q1==q2: True

checks.claim: Query cache returns wrong results due to hash collision
checks.evidence: python -c "from tinydb import TinyDB, where; db=TinyDB(':memory:'); db.insert_multiple([{'name':n} for n in ['Alice','Alan','bob']]); r1=db.search(where('name').startswith('Al')); r2=db.search(where('name').startswith('Bo')); print('Al:', [d['name'] for d in r1], 'Bo:', [d['name'] for d in r2])" -> both return ['Alice','Alan']

findings.text: startswith hashval tuple ('startswith', self._path) doesn't include the prefix parameter, causing different prefixes to have identical hashes and be considered equal
endswith hashval tuple ('endswith', self._path) doesn't include the suffix parameter, causing the same cache collision bug
Tests don't cover the caching bug - they only test basic functionality, not that different prefixes produce different query objects
